# Direction of Benefit and Clinical Margins {#sec-benefit-direction-margins}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Make difference direction explicit.
- Relate clinical margins to outcomes and target effects.
:::

## The idea

Before choosing a directional objective, define the group order (for example, new minus standard) and outcome desirability. Higher survival or recovery scores may be favourable, while lower blood pressure or complication risk may be favourable. Reversing group order changes the sign of the effect and requires a corresponding conversion of margins.

## When and how to apply it

A margin is not selected merely because the resulting sample size is manageable. Its justification should address clinical consequences, comparability with previous evidence, measurement scale and population. Planning plots can expose how sensitive the sample size is to the chosen margin.

## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
A non-inferiority margin of +5 mmHg may be interpretable when lower blood pressure is better, whereas a recovery endpoint may use a negative margin under new-minus-control coding.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
Input errors in “higher is better” settings can invert the clinical meaning of a hypothesis.
:::
